FlowMap

Geometry-aware vector field embeddings for RNA velocity and dynamical analysis.

Core API

class flowmap.Spline(X: ndarray, n_control_points: int | None = 1000, max_n: int = 4000)[source]

Bases: object

Polyharmonic spline regression model (2D triharmonic spline).

This model represents a smooth mapping

f : ℝᵈ → ℝᴰ

of the form:

f(x) = Σᵢ wᵢ φ(||x - cᵢ||) + P₂(x) a

where:

  • φ(r) = r⁴ log r (polyharmonic kernel of order m=3 in 2D)

  • cᵢ are control points

  • wᵢ are radial weights

  • P₂(x) contains all monomials up to degree 2

  • a are polynomial coefficients

The radial weights are ridge-regularized.

This spline is C² smooth and suitable for:

  • Jacobian computation

  • Hessian computation

  • Riemannian metric construction

  • Curvature and torsion analysis

  • Velocity pushforwards

Parameters:

  • X (ndarray of shape (N, d)) – Input training points.

  • n_control_points (int, optional (default=1000)) – Number of control points. If larger than N, all points are used.

  • max_n (int, optional (default=4000)) – Warning threshold for large datasets.

Notes

For polyharmonic splines of order m=3 in 2D, the polynomial tail must have degree m-1 = 2.

References

Duchon (1977), Splines minimizing rotation-invariant seminorms.

compute_christoffels(evaluation_points: ndarray, eps: float = 1e-08) → ndarray[source]

Compute Christoffel symbols of the induced connection.

Using:

Γ^k_{ij} = g^{km} ⟨∂²f/∂x_i∂x_j , ∂f/∂x_m⟩

Parameters:

  • evaluation_points (ndarray of shape (M, d))

  • eps (float, optional) – Numerical stability parameter.

Returns:

Christoffel symbols Γ^k_{ij} at each point.

Return type:

ndarray of shape (M, d, d, d)

Notes

These define the Levi-Civita connection induced by the embedding f.

compute_dof(lambda_reg: float) → float[source]

Compute effective degrees of freedom (DoF) of the spline model.

The radial contribution is computed from the singular values of the kernel matrix Φ:

dof_radial = Σ_i s_i² / (s_i² + λ)

where s_i are singular values of Φ.

The polynomial contribution equals the number of polynomial basis functions (degree 2):

dof_poly = C(d+2, 2)

Parameters:

lambda_reg (float) – Ridge regularization parameter λ.

Returns:

Effective degrees of freedom.

Return type:

float

Notes

This corresponds to the trace of the smoothing matrix for ridge-regularized RBF regression.

compute_hessians(evaluation_points: ndarray, eps: float = 1e-12) → ndarray[source]

Compute Hessian matrices of the spline mapping.

For φ(r)=r^4 log r, with s = ||x-c||^2 and d = x-c:

∇²φ = 2(2 log s + 3) ddᵀ + s(2 log s + 1) I

with ∇²φ(0)=0.

Return type:

ndarray of shape (M, D, d, d)

compute_jacobians(evaluation_points: ndarray, eps: float = 1e-12) → ndarray[source]

Compute Jacobian matrices of the spline mapping.

For φ(r) = r^4 log r, using s = ||x-c||^2:

∇φ = (x - c) * s * (2 log s + 1)

with ∇φ(0) = 0.

Return type:

ndarray of shape (M, D, d)

compute_metric(evaluation_points: ndarray, eps: float = 1e-08) → ndarray[source]

Compute induced Riemannian metric tensor.

Given Jacobians J(x), the metric is:

g_ij = ⟨∂f/∂x_i , ∂f/∂x_j⟩

Parameters:

  • evaluation_points (ndarray of shape (M, d))

  • eps (float, optional) – Numerical stability parameter.

Returns:

Metric tensor at each evaluation point.

Return type:

ndarray of shape (M, d, d)

compute_torsion(evaluation_points: ndarray, eps: float = 1e-08) → ndarray[source]

Compute torsion tensor.

T^k_{ij} = Γ^k_{ij} − Γ^k_{ji}

For a Levi-Civita connection, torsion should vanish.

Parameters:

evaluation_points (ndarray of shape (M, d))

Returns:

Torsion tensor.

Return type:

ndarray of shape (M, d, d, d)

map_velocities(V: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Project velocity vectors through the spline tangent.

Given velocities V in output space, this computes their representation in input coordinates using:

J(x) v_input ≈ v_output

via least squares.

Parameters:

V (ndarray of shape (N, D)) – Velocity vectors in embedding space.

Returns:

Mapped velocities in input coordinates.

Return type:

ndarray of shape (N, d)

Notes

This implements a local pseudo-inverse of the Jacobian.

predict(X_new: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Evaluate the fitted spline at new input locations.

This computes the mapping

f(x) = Σ_i w_i φ(||x - c_i||) + P₂(x) a

where:

  • φ(r) = r⁴ log r

  • c_i are control points

  • P₂(x) is the quadratic polynomial basis

Parameters:

X_new (ndarray of shape (M, d) or (d,)) – Evaluation points in input space.

Returns:

Predicted outputs. If a single point is provided, a 1D array is returned.

Return type:

ndarray of shape (M, D) or (D,)

Notes

Internally computes:

  • pairwise distances to control points

  • radial basis evaluation

  • polynomial tail evaluation

The method assumes the spline has been fitted.

class flowmap.VectorFieldEmbedder(X: ndarray, V: ndarray, *, method: str = 'umap', embedding_dim: int = 2, dof: float = 30, dof_vf: float | None = None, dist_method: str = 'phase', custom_dist: ndarray | None = None, X_emb: ndarray | None = None, dist_kwargs: dict | None = None, embed_kwargs: dict | None = None, spline_kwargs: dict | None = None, spline_vf_kwargs: dict | None = None, knn_k: int = 30, alpha: float = 0.5, use_PCA: bool = True, pca_components: int = 30, max_spline_points: int = 4000)[source]

Bases: object

Geometry-aware embedding for vector field data.

Parameters:

  • X (ndarray (N, d)) – High-dimensional data.

  • V (ndarray (N, d)) – Vector field in input space.

  • method ({"umap", "tsne", "pca"}) – Embedding method.

  • dist_method ({"phase", "euclidean"}) – Distance computation method.

  • dof (float) – Degrees of freedom for geometry spline.

  • dof_vf (float) – Degrees of freedom for vector-field spline.

Notes

The pipeline:

X –(embedding)–> X_emb X_emb –(Spline)–> X X –(pushforward)–> V_emb

Two splines are fitted:

  1. Geometry spline : embedding → input space

  2. Velocity spline : embedding → embedded vector field

fit_embedding(seed: int | None = None) → None[source]

Compute the initial embedding and fit geometry-aware splines.

This method performs:

  1. Distance graph computation (if using phase distance)

  2. Low-dimensional embedding (e.g. UMAP / t-SNE / PCA)

  3. Spline fitting:

    • spline : Spline

    • spline_vf : Spline

Parameters:

seed (int, optional) – Random seed for reproducibility.

Notes

After calling this method, the following attributes are available:

  • X_embndarray (N, embedding_dim)

    Embedded coordinates.

  • V_embndarray (N, embedding_dim)

    Embedded vector field.

  • spline : Spline

  • spline_vf : Spline

This method must be called before refine_embedding().

fit_gene_level_splines(dof_gene: float = 30, dof_vf_gene: float = 30, X: ndarray | None = None, V: ndarray | None = None) → None[source]

Fit gene-level splines for expression and velocity fields.

This method constructs separate splines mapping:

embedding → gene expression embedding → gene-level velocity

Parameters:

  • dof_gene (float, default=30) – Degrees of freedom for gene-expression spline.

  • dof_vf_gene (float, default=30) – Degrees of freedom for gene-velocity spline.

  • X (ndarray (N, p), optional) – Gene expression matrix. If None, uses raw input data.

  • V (ndarray (N, p), optional) – Gene velocity matrix. If None, uses raw input velocities.

Notes

Three cases:

  1. Custom gene matrices provided → fit new splines.

  2. No custom input → use raw high-dimensional data.

  3. If no gene refitting is desired, splines are reused.

After fitting, the following attributes are set:

  • spline_gene

  • spline_vf_gene

  • X_gene

  • V_gene

refine_embedding(lam: float | None = None, method: str = 'batch', batch_size: int = 64, lr: float = 0.001, epochs: int = 50, tol: float = 0.01, verbose: bool = False) → None[source]

Refine the embedding using geometry-aware optimization.

This is an optional iterative refinement step that adjusts embedding coordinates to improve geometric consistency between:

  • the spline reconstruction

  • the vector field alignment

Parameters:

  • method ({"batch", "global"}) –

    Optimization strategy:

    • ”batch” : stochastic mini-batch refinement (SGD)

    • ”global” : full-batch optimization

  • batch_size (int) – Mini-batch size (for batch mode).

  • lr (float) – Learning rate (batch mode).

  • epochs (int) – Number of optimization epochs (batch mode).

  • tol (float) – Tolerance for convergence (global mode).

  • verbose (bool) – Whether to print optimization progress.

Notes

This method:

  1. Updates X_emb

  2. Re-fits geometry and velocity splines

  3. Updates V_emb accordingly

static classify_fixed_point(J: ndarray, eps: float = 0.0001) → str[source]

Classify a fixed point using linear stability analysis of its Jacobian.

The classification is determined from the eigenvalue spectrum of the Jacobian matrix evaluated at the fixed point.

Parameters:

  • J (ndarray of shape (d, d)) – Jacobian matrix of the vector field at the fixed point.

  • eps (float, default=1e-4) – Numerical tolerance used to determine whether eigenvalues are considered zero or have non-negligible imaginary parts.

Returns:

One of:

  • ”Stable node (sink)”

  • ”Unstable node (source)”

  • ”Saddle”

  • ”Degenerate”

  • ”Center”

  • ”Spiral in”

  • ”Spiral out”

  • ”Mixed focus”

Return type:

str

Notes

Let \(\lambda_i \in \mathbb{C}\) denote the eigenvalues of J.

  • Stability is determined by the sign of \(\Re(\lambda_i)\).

  • Purely real spectra correspond to node or saddle behavior.

  • Complex conjugate pairs indicate rotational (spiral or center) dynamics.

  • A fixed point is:

    • Stable if all \(\Re(\lambda_i) < 0\)

    • Unstable if all \(\Re(\lambda_i) > 0\)

    • A saddle if signs are mixed

This classification corresponds to the local linearization of the dynamical system near the fixed point.

class flowmap.geometry.GeneGradientAnalyzer(emb)[source]

Bases: object

Analyze gene-level gradients in embedding space.

This class evaluates the geometry of gene-expression gradients reconstructed via the gene-level spline.

For each cell, the spline Jacobian provides:

J(z) = ∂X_gene / ∂z

Combined with the pullback metric, this allows computing:

  • Riemannian gradients

  • Alignment with local velocity

  • Parallel / orthogonal components

No plotting is performed here. Visualization should be handled in the plotting module.

class flowmap.geometry.LagrangianPathOptimizer(embedding, D: float = 1.0, lam: float = 0.0)[source]

Bases: object

Minimum-action path computation for FlowMap embeddings.

This class computes transition trajectories under the action:

\[S[x] = \frac{1}{2D} \int ||\dot{x} - v(x)||^2 dt + \lambda \int ||\dot{x}||^2 dt\]

where:

  • v(x) is the embedded vector field

  • D is the diffusion constant

  • λ is an arc-length regularization weight

The optimizer:

  1. Initializes a path via Dijkstra on a kNN graph

  2. Refines the path by gradient descent on the action functional

fit_path(start: ndarray, end: ndarray, *, distance_mode: str = 'embed', subsample_n: int = 4000, k: int = 20, alpha: float = 0.0, n_segments: int = 100, lr: float = 0.005, iters: int = 300) → Dict[source]

Compute minimum-action transition path between two states.

Parameters:

  • end (ndarray (d,)) – Ending coordinate.

  • distance_mode ({"embed", "orig"}) – Graph geometry for initialization.

  • subsample_n (int) – Number of points used for graph.

  • k (int) – Number of nearest neighbors.

  • alpha (float) – Velocity-alignment weight.

  • n_segments (int) – Number of discretization segments.

  • lr (float) – Gradient descent learning rate.

  • iters (int) – Number of refinement iterations.

Returns:

  • path_init

  • path_refined

  • dt

Return type:

dict with keys

class flowmap.evaluation.SplineFitEvaluator(emb, *, mode: str | None = None, cell_idx: ndarray | None = None)[source]

Bases: object

Evaluate reconstruction accuracy of manifold and velocity splines.

This class quantifies how well a fitted spline model reconstructs:

  1. Feature values (e.g. genes or principal components)

  2. Vector field values

It supports evaluation at two levels:

  • Gene-level splines (spline_gene, spline_vf_gene)

  • Embedding-level splines (spline, spline_vf)

If mode is not specified, gene-level splines are used when available; otherwise embedding-level splines are evaluated.

Notes

Let \(f(z)\) denote the spline mapping from embedding coordinates \(z\) to feature space, and let \(J(z) = \nabla f(z)\) denote its Jacobian.

Expression reconstruction is evaluated via:

\[R^2 = 1 - \frac{\|X - \hat{X}\|^2}{\|X - \bar{X}\|^2}\]

Velocity reconstruction is evaluated using the local linear pushforward:

\[\hat{V} = J(z) \beta,\]

where \(\beta\) is obtained by least-squares fitting to the observed velocity.

This provides both global and per-feature metrics.

evaluate() → Dict[source]

Compute reconstruction metrics.

Returns:

Dictionary containing:

expr_r2float

Mean expression R² across features.

vel_r2float

Mean velocity R² across features.

expr_r2_genelist of float

Per-feature expression R² values.

vel_r2_genelist of float

Per-feature velocity R² values.

expr_corr_genelist of float

Per-feature Pearson correlation (expression).

vel_corr_genelist of float

Per-feature Pearson correlation (velocity).

X_predndarray

Reconstructed feature values.

V_predndarray

Reconstructed velocity values.

Return type:

dict

Notes

Expression reconstruction evaluates the spline prediction:

\[\hat{X} = f(z)\]

Velocity reconstruction evaluates the local linear pushforward:

\[\hat{V} = J(z) \beta\]

where \(\beta\) is obtained via least-squares fit at each cell independently.

flowmap.plot.plot_velocity_grid(X_emb, spline_vf=None, V=None, grid_size=50, grid_density=1.0, smooth=0.5, n_neighbors=None, min_mass=0.01, scatter_color=None, scatter_size=80, scatter_alpha=0.1, arrow_color='black', arrow_alpha=0.9, arrow_scale=3.0, arrow_width=0.0025, figsize=(6, 6), cmap='viridis', vmin=None, vmax=None, show_axes=False, show_colorbar=False)[source]

Plot a 2D velocity field as quiver arrows evaluated on a grid.

This visualization evaluates a smooth vector field on a masked rectilinear grid and displays it using matplotlib’s quiver plot.

Parameters:

  • X_emb ((n, 2) array) – 2D embedding coordinates.

  • spline_vf (Spline, optional) – Pre-fitted flowmap.spline.Spline model. If None, a spline is fitted from V.

  • V ((n, 2) array, optional) – Raw velocity vectors corresponding to X_emb. Required if spline_vf is None.

  • grid_size (int) – Resolution of the evaluation grid.

  • grid_density (float) – Multiplier controlling grid sampling density.

  • smooth (float) – Density smoothing parameter used for grid masking.

  • min_mass (float) – Threshold for masking low-density grid regions.

  • arrow_scale (float) – Scaling factor controlling quiver arrow length.

  • arrow_width (float) – Width of quiver arrows.

Notes

  • Grid construction and masking are handled by flowmap.utils.compute_velocity_on_grid.

  • Designed for RNA velocity visualization but applicable to any 2D vector field.
